title: How long does fish last in the freezer?

seo.title: How long does fish last in the freezer?
seo.meta_description: USDA lists 3–8 months for best quality for frozen raw fish and about 3 months for cooked fish. At 0 °F, safety lasts longer than peak quality.
seo.search_intent: Learn how long frozen fish keeps good quality and how species, fat and packaging affect freezer life.

excerpt: USDA recommends using frozen raw fish within about 3–8 months for best quality and cooked fish within about 3 months. Fish kept continuously at 0 °F remains safe longer, but flavor and texture gradually decline.
content_html:
Freezing stops bacterial growth, but it does not preserve peak texture forever. USDA lists 3–8 months for raw fish and about 3 months for cooked fish as best-quality targets.

Safety and quality are different

Fish kept continuously at 0 °F (−18 °C) remains safe beyond those quality windows. Over time, oxidation, dehydration and freezer burn affect flavor and texture.

Why is the raw-fish range so wide?

Species and fat content matter. Oily fish tend to develop oxidized flavors sooner than very lean fish, so using the shorter end of the range for salmon, mackerel or sardines is sensible, while well-wrapped lean fish may hold quality longer.

Packaging matters

Air exposure accelerates oxidation and freezer burn. Use freezer-grade packaging, remove excess air and freeze in portions sized for one use.

What about cooked fish?

USDA gives roughly 3 months for best quality of cooked fish. Sauced dishes may behave differently, but fish texture still declines with long storage.

Fish can lose quality while still being within a guideline

Freezer timelines are not expiration dates. A poorly wrapped fillet can develop freezer burn and oxidized flavors well before three months, while a well-protected one may hold quality for longer. The date and the condition of the package therefore need to be read together.

For thawing, the refrigerator gives the simplest control. Dry or pale patches caused by freezer burn are mainly a quality problem; spending too long thawing at room temperature is a separate food-safety issue.

Use 3–8 months for raw fish and about 3 months for cooked fish as quality windows, not exact safety expiration dates.

faq.question: Does frozen fish become unsafe after 8 months?
faq.answer: Not automatically if continuously held at 0 °F; 3–8 months is mainly a best-quality range for raw fish.

faq.question: How long does cooked fish last frozen?
faq.answer: USDA recommends about 3 months for best quality.

faq.question: Do fatty fish keep for less time?
faq.answer: They often lose quality sooner because their fats oxidize more readily, so shorter storage is preferable.
